title: US Market Week Ahead: October CPI and AI Earnings in Focus
summary: October CPI, PPI and earnings from CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco lead the US market agenda for November 9-13, 2026.
body_markdown:
For PPI, FXEmpire lists a forecast of a 0.4% monthly increase. Together, the two reports will show whether price pressures are easing or holding firm.


Thursday's jobless claims will round out the labor market picture. A continued low reading would reinforce the view that the US economy is not slowing.


The Fed backdrop raises the stakes. On October 28, the Fed held its policy rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, with two FOMC members voting for a 25 basis point hike.


According to FXEmpire, futures markets now price roughly an 80% chance of a hike at the December 8-9 meeting. A CPI print that misses forecasts in either direction could move that expectation sharply.


Several Fed officials are also scheduled to speak, according to the Federal Reserve Board's official calendar:


- Tuesday, November 10: Governor Christopher Waller and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman, both on the economic outlook.
- Thursday, November 12: Governor Michael Barr on artificial intelligence and inequality.
- Friday, November 13: Vice Chair Philip Jefferson on productivity and new technology.


Their remarks may offer further hints on policy once the CPI numbers are out.


## This Week's Earnings Calendar


Third-quarter earnings season is in its final stretch. According to FactSet as of November 6, 2026, 88% of S&P 500 companies have reported and the blended Q3 earnings growth rate stands at 31.4%.


Here is when some of the week's larger companies report, with consensus EPS estimates from Nasdaq.com:


- [Constellation Energy (CEG)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ceg/) , Monday, November 9, before the open: EPS of US$3.90. The market will read the report for signs of power demand from data centers.
- [Occidental Petroleum (OXY)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/oxy/) , Monday, November 9, after the close: EPS of US$1.43. Production volumes and the impact of oil prices are the focus.
- [CoreWeave (CRWV)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/crwv/) , Tuesday, November 10, after the close: a loss of US$1.45 per share. Contract backlog and data center capital spending plans will be in focus.
- [Applied Materials (AMAT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amat/) , Thursday, November 12, after the close: EPS of US$4.06. The market will read it for chip equipment demand, including for AI and memory.


Other reports scheduled this week:


- [Take-Two Interactive (TTWO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ttwo/) and[Rocket Lab (RKLB)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/rklb/) , Monday, November 9, after the close.
- [Sea Limited (SE)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/se/) , Tuesday, November 10, before the open.
- [Nebius (NBIS)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nbis/) , Thursday, November 12, before the open.
- [Cisco (CSCO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/csco/) , Thursday, November 12, after the close, with attention on networking orders tied to AI infrastructure.


For the AI trade, the CoreWeave and Applied Materials reports arrive at a sensitive moment. Both will be read as clues to whether data center spending is holding up through the tech pullback.


## Market Sentiment


The main story right now is a retest of the AI trade. Investors are asking how quickly heavy data center spending can turn into profit.


At the same time, the US economy remains strong and inflation has not fully cooled. That mix has put the risk of another Fed rate hike back at the center of the conversation.


US Treasury yields tend to react quickly to inflation data. Rising yields often weigh on tech valuations, which lean heavily on future earnings growth.


FXEmpire also points to political risk. Democratic gains in Congress and in key governors' races could bring tighter rules and permitting delays for data center construction.


In this setting, volatility may pick up around the CPI release and the AI-linked earnings reports. Here are the two main scenarios to prepare for:


- CPI below forecast: pressure for a rate hike could ease, and sentiment toward tech may improve.
- CPI above forecast: the case for a December hike strengthens, and volatility could continue.


With most S&P 500 companies already reported, attention is likely to shift toward macro data. The Fed's policy path may become the main driver over the next few weeks.


Strong S&P 500 earnings growth is still supporting the market. This week should show whether investors focus on fundamentals or on interest rate risk.


Keep an eye on each release and make decisions that fit your own risk profile.
